On ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'', Britney made close relationships with [[Lane Elenburg]], [[Monet Stunson]], and [[Ragan Fox]], while getting into a rivalry with [[Brendon Villegas]] and [[Rachel Reilly]]. However, she was infamously unaware that she was helping to push the agendas of the secret dominant alliance, [[The Brigade]]. At the final four, she became the consensus target for being the only non-Brigade member left. After failing to win the [[Head of Household]] and [[Power of Veto]], the Brigade revealed the existence of their alliance and her imminent eviction to a shocked Britney, with [[Enzo Palumbo]] casting the sole vote to evict her. She placed 4th and was the 6th member of the [[The Jury|jury]]. On finale night, she won the [[America's Favorite Houseguest]] award. Britney returned on ''[[Big Brother 14 (US)]]'', as a [[Coach]]. Although initially in a minority position as she only had one player left in [[Shane Meaney]], she was able to pull through with her excellent social positioning with the rest of the house. However, when the coaches were allowed to enter the game as players in week 3, Britney became a key member of [[The Quack Pack]] alliance, forming strong relationships with [[Danielle Murphree]] and [[Ian Terry]]. Her game came to an end at the final eight when [[Dan Gheesling]] managed to miraculously get himself off the block at the Power of Veto ceremony by revealing [[Ian Terry]]'s duplicity to Dan's nemesis [[Frank Eudy]]. As Ian was safe for winning a second veto, Dan convinced Frank to target Britney as collateral damage instead, in an attempt to weaken Ian and eliminate a huge strategic threat. She was evicted in a 4 to 1 vote, with Ian being the sole vote to keep her. She placed 8th and was the second member of the jury. On ''Reindeer Games'', Britney quickly made amends with [[Nicole Franzel]], her friend with whom she had a falling out with outside the game, and forged an unbreakable alliance with her, along with ''[[Big Brother 16 (US)|Big Brother 16]]'' contestant [[Frankie Grande]]. With her social relationships and challenge performances, she was able to avoid elimination and take out several physical threats. She also further was the direct reason of [[Danielle Reyes]]' memorable elimination. Eventually, Britney was eliminated at the penultimate episode as she narrowly lost to [[Xavier Prather]] at the Santa's Showdown and barely missed out the chance to be at the titular Reindeer Games finale. Britney is known for her snarky sense of humor and quick wit. She garnered widespread attention and praise for her [[Diary Room]] commentary, with one of her comments making the Emmys. Her natural ability to make everyone laugh helped her become a fan favorite, and she is also considered by many as one of the show's greatest social players.

He later competed on ''[[Big Brother: Reindeer Games]]''. Cody played one of the strongest social and strategic games of ''Big Brother 16'', beginning as a founding member of the dominant [[Bomb Squad]] alliance before helping form [[The Detonators]]. He became a key member of the majority alliance, winning multiple competitions while maintaining strong relationships that kept him safe throughout the game.Cody found himself a loyal ally in [[Derrick Levasseur]] and together they formed a game-lasting Final Two alliance called [[The Hitmen]]. Cody won several Head of Household competitions, including the final HOH, and consistently helped eliminate outsiders. After he won the final HOH, Cody chose to infamously evict [[Victoria Rafaeli]] and take his fellow Hitmen Derrick with him to the Final Two. Despite the strong social connections he made throughout the game, Cody was criticized for blindly following Derrick’s plans and lost in a 7–2 jury vote, finishing as the runner-up. Cody's decision to evict Victoria has been considered one of the worst moves ever by the viewers because they believe he could have easily won against Victoria. Most of the jurors have even admitted that Cody would have beaten Victoria. Cody began ''Big Brother 22'' by winning the first HoH. Following his win, both he and [[Memphis Garrett]] formed a final 2 alliance called [[The Commission]], and the two brought in other houseguests into their alliance called [[The Committee]]. The Committee controlled the season, which kept Cody safe. Cody had several alliances and deals, such as separate final 2 deals with Memphis, [[Enzo Palumbo]] and fellow BB16 castmate [[Nicole Franzel]], as well as a final 3 alliance with Enzo and Memphis called The Wise guys. Cody had a hand in evicting several players, including his own allies. He was a competition threat again, winning 4 HoH's and 4 PoV's. He was in alliances with almost everyone in the house, and developed very strong friendships with Enzo, Nicole F, Memphis and [[Daniele Briones]], but had a minor dislike towards [[David Alexander]], short lived running feuds with [[Janelle Pierzina]] and [[Kevin Campbell]] and a long running-feud with [[Kaysar Ridha]]. Cody managed not to be nominated throughout the season and after winning the Final HoH, he became the first ever houseguest to make it to the final 2 without ever going on the block. Cody's dominant strategic and social games, and competition wins earned him the win in a unanimous 9-0 vote. By having no eviction votes cast against him and receiving all the jury votes, he became the second American houseguest to play a [[Perfect Game]], after [[Dan Gheesling]] on ''Big Brother 10''. Returning on ''Reindeer Games'', Cody found himself reunited with his ''Big Brother 16'' castmates [[Frankie Grande]], whom he easily connected with for their friendship outside the game and reaffirmed their alliance together, and Nicole, with whom he was wary about for his last-minute betrayal when he evicted her at the finale of ''Big Brother 22''. Quickly, Cody saw himself targeted by other people, most notably by [[Taylor Hale]], for being a threat. Winning the Naughty and Nice Challenge, Cody won the advantage of forming his own team for the upcoming Jingle Bell Brawl and cobbled the physical powerhouses in a bid to win the team immunity. However, his team lost and was placed in Santa's Showdown, which ultimately sent Cody home, marking the first and only time he was eliminated in all of his ''Big Brother'' appearances. In his first two appearances, Cody has placed 2nd and 1st, which is currently tied for the best result in two appearances in the game. He is the third player to make it to the Final Two twice.

He also appeared on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]''. In ''Big Brother 12'', Enzo became well-known for his use of his moniker "the meow-meow" and was the founding member of [[The Brigade]]. Enzo played a social, under-the-radar strategic game early on, focusing on long-term positioning rather than being an immediate target. While he rarely won competitions in the early and middle stages, he maintained strong loyalty within his alliance and consistently avoided becoming a primary eviction threat as the Brigade systematically controlled votes. As the he reached the endgame, Enzo continued relying on alliance strength and timing, ensuring that more visible threats were removed ahead of him, and his allegiance to the Brigade helped him make it to the final three. Enzo ultimately placed 3rd after [[Hayden Moss]] cast the sole vote to evict him, thus making him the seventh and final member of the [[jury]]. In ''Big Brother 22'', Enzo found himself in a comfortable position as an affiliate of [[The Committee]] alliance. He was particularly close with Committee members [[Cody Calafiore]] and [[Memphis Garrett]], having a final 3 deal with them called the Wise Guys, and a final 2 alliance with Cody called [[The Root]]. He proved to be better in competitions this time around, winning 2 HoH's, 1 PoV, and 1 Safety competition. He overall made very safe moves, nominating obvious target Kaysar, and also keeping [[Nicole Franzel]] over [[David Alexander]] in final 8. He made it to the final three without being nominated. After Cody won the final HoH, he brought Enzo to the final two. He had a dislike towards [[Kaysar Ridha]] and successfully got him evicted in Week 4, and clashed with [[Janelle Pierzina]] over their conflicting personalities, but developed friendships with [[Bayleigh Dayton]], Nicole F, [[Christmas Abbott]], [[Daniele Briones]], [[Da'Vonne Rogers]], including stronger ones with Cody, [[Tyler Crispen]] and [[Memphis Garrett]]. However, Enzo's subtle game wasn't respected for Cody's dominant and aggressive game, and he gave poor answers to the jury's questions. This caused him to finish second to Cody in a unanimous 9-0 vote, making Enzo the second ever houseguest to receive 0 jury votes, after Memphis.

After Victor re-entered the game, the pair formed the [[The Sitting Ducks]] alliance and remained close until late in the game, when both were nominated and Paul survived while Victor was evicted. A strong strategic and social player, Paul controlled much of the endgame through competition wins and manipulation, ultimately winning multiple HOHs and POVs to reach the final two. After winning the final HOH, they chose to evict James instead of Nicole, a decision widely viewed as a critical mistake. Paul was considered a very aggressive player, being unafraid to make big moves, willing to confront others, and having a hand in numerous evictions. Paul was known for being able to talk their way out of many situations and for playing a great social and strategic game. However, they received criticism for insulting other HouseGuests, making many jury members lose respect for their gameplay. Paul ultimately lost the game in a 5–4 jury vote, finishing as runner-up. Paul later returned for ''Big Brother 19'' with a heavily altered strategy, focusing more on manipulation and social control than pure competition wins. Paul used their early safety through a Week 1 twist and the Pendant of Protection to build relationships and navigate early nominations, while gradually positioning themself at the center of house decisions and forming key bonds. Despite multiple attempts to target them, Paul remained off the block until the final three due to strong gameplay, competition wins, and strategic influence over evictions. However, Paul's aggressive and controversial social style, including perceived manipulation and jury mismanagement, ultimately cost them the win, and they were narrowly defeated 5–4 by [[Josh Martinez]], finishing as runner-up for the second consecutive season. Along with [[Danielle Reyes]] and [[Dan Gheesling|Dan]], Paul is considered to be another victim of a bitter jury; despite what majority of viewers perceived as a stronger game than the actual winner. Paul has won the most competitions in Big Brother history with 14 wins over their two seasons. Due to this and making final 2 twice, Paul has been seen as one of the greatest players in recent years, comparing them to Big Brother legends [[Derrick Levasseur]] and [[Vanessa Rousso]].

She also competed on ''[[Big Brother 12 (US)]]'' and ''[[Big Brother 27 (US)]]''. In ''Big Brother 12 (US)'', Rachel a strong and outspoken competitor, quickly forming a showmance with [[Brendon Villegas]] and becoming an early target of [[The Brigade]] due to her overbearing personality. After Hayden nominated them in the first week, Brendon won the Power of Veto and saved himself, allowing Rachel to avoid eviction as [[Annie Whittington]] was sent home instead. Rachel won two early Head of Household competitions, using her first HOH to evict [[Monet Stunson]] and later targeting [[Hayden Moss]] and [[Kristen Bitting]], which exposed tension between her and the house. Despite her competition ability and loyalty to Brendon, Rachel struggled socially and was repeatedly viewed as a threat, especially by The Brigade. After [[Matt Hoffman]] nominated Rachel and Brendon during his HOH in Week 5, she fought to stay. However, when [[Britney Haynes]] won the Power of Veto and chose not to use it, Rachel was unanimously evicted on Day 41 for being seen as the more significant threat of the duo. She placed 9th and was the first member of the [[jury]]. She would cast her jury vote for [[Lane Elenburg]], feeling he had played the best social game. She returned to the game in ''Big Brother 13 (US)'' as part of the [[Dynamic Duos|dynamic duo]] twist, being partnered with her then fiancé, now husband, Brendon Villegas. Rachel immediately established herself as a major threat by winning two Head of Household competitions early on and leading the [[Veterans]] alliance after [[Dick Donato]] walked from the game. After the Veterans alliance fractured due to [[Daniele Briones|Daniele Briones']] attempt to backdoor fellow veterans [[Jeff Schroeder]] and [[Jordan Lloyd]], Rachel became a target and was nominated alongside Brendon by Daniele in Week 4; Brendon saved her with the Power of Veto but was evicted. Rachel survived the block in Week 5 and Brendon returned through a battle back twist, but he was soon evicted again, leaving her and the remaining veterans vulnerable. She survived a double eviction that sent Jeff out, then won the final five HoH and used her position to eliminate [[Kalia Booker]]. After reaching the Final 3 with [[Porsche Briggs]] and [[Adam Poch]], Rachel won the final HoH, evicted Adam, and defeated Porsche 4-3 in the jury vote to win the $500,000 grand prize, completing a comeback victory after being targeted throughout the game. In ''Big Brother 27 (US)'', Rachel was the sole returning player and her presence dominated the first half of the season. Throughout her time in the game, she made tight bonds with [[Amy Bingham]], [[Ashley Hollis]], and [[Jimmy Heagerty]], while also developing season-long rivalries with [[Keanu Soto]] and [[Vince Panaro]]. Despite her massive target, Rachel managed to avoid being nominated during her time in the house by insulating herself well and being used as a shield by other players. Unfortunately for Rachel, her luck ran out when she failed to complete the [[Hit The Road]] competition in the allotted time at the White Locust Resort, resulting in her abrupt exit from the game on Day 60 and becoming the first member of the jury. Rachel's exit this season was the source of much controversy, especially since she managed to avoid being nominated up to that point in the game. Despite her constant irritation to other houseguests and viewers often due to her grating laugh and frequent crying, she and Brendon ("Brenchel") developed a huge fan base. Due to her competition prowess, she is considered one of the greatest physical players in the show's history, having won every endurance competition she has competed in.

Even though he drew the ire of many of his fellow houseguests and was nominated four times through the season, Will was able to stay in the game with the help of his charismatic personality, clever social maneuvers, and over the top strategies, making the target on his back so big that he was able to hide in plain sight. While he failed to win the final Head of Household, he was taken to the final 2 by [[Nicole Nilson Schaffrich]]. At the end of the jury questionnaire, Will rubbed many of the [[Jury|jurors]] the wrong way with his final jury speech. Despite this, most of the jury respected Will's game, and he won the $500,000 grand prize by a 5-2 [[Jury|jury]] vote over Nicole. On ''Big Brother 7 (US)'', Will entered the house with a huge target on his back due to being the only winner in the game. However, with the help of fellow ''Big Brother 2'' housemate and "Chilltown" member Mike "Boogie", Will was able to manipulate other houseguests (most notably his new showmance parter [[Janelle Pierzina]]) and managed to get rid of big names like [[Howie Gordon]], [[James Rhine]], and [[Danielle Reyes]] just to name a few. Will's ultimate demise was during the final 4 when [[Erika Landin]] and Janelle caught onto Chilltown's schemes. Since Mike "Boogie" was the HOH of that week and could not be evicted, Janelle, the Power of Veto holder of that week, casted the sole vote to evict Will from the house, making him the 6th member of the jury. At the finale, Will voted for his ally Mike "Boogie" to win the game.
